reading.body:
CyrusOne Florence (CIN6) publishes 5 MW of IT capacity across 143,000 square feet, the largest disclosed data center campus in Kentucky by capacity.

The facility accounts for more than half of Kentucky's published data center IT capacity, which totals 9.55 MW across three facilities with disclosed figures. Five mapped facilities exist in the state, but most do not publish power specifications, so the true installed base is likely larger than the disclosed total. At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks, a scale consistent with enterprise and cloud tenants rather than a purpose-built AI training campus.

Certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes qualify the site for regulated workloads, but none of that indicates AI-specific retrofit plans, local grid capacity, or expansion commitments. The published specifications omit the power and building changes required to convert this conventional facility into a higher-density GPU deployment, so its relevance to AI scaling remains unproven.
